I've gathered substantial material from several key commentaries. Let me now compile the verse-by-verse notes. Due to search/fetch limits, I was unable to retrieve dedicated Catholic, Orthodox, Lutheran, and Methodist sources. I will mark those as "not found" where applicable.

---

## Revelation 14 — Verse-by-Verse Commentary Notes

### Overview of the Chapter

John Gill (Baptist, 18th century) outlines three visions: (1) the Lamb on Mount Zion with the 144,000, (2) three angels preaching against Babylon, and (3) the harvest and vintage. [biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/revelation/14.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/revelation/14.htm)

Ellicott (Anglican) notes there are seven agents in the chapter: the angel of good news (vv. 6–7), the angel proclaiming Babylon's doom (v. 8), the angel warning about the mark (vv. 9–12), the angel of comfort (v. 13), the angel of the wheat harvest (vv. 14–16), the angel of the vintage (vv. 17–20), and the angel of fire (v. 18). [biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/14.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/14.htm)

David Guzik (Enduring Word, charismatic/evangelical) says the chapter answers two questions raised by Revelation 13: "Is the beast completely victorious over all God's people?" (answer: no, the 144,000 stand triumphant), and "What happens to the beast and his followers?" (answer: they face the winepress of God's wrath). [enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-14/](https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-14/)

---

### v. 1: "Then I looked and saw the Lamb standing on Mount Zion, and with Him 144,000 who had His name and His Father's name written on their foreheads."

**Traditional readings:**

- **Gill:** The Lamb is Christ, the same as in Revelation 5:6. Mount Zion means the church on earth, not heaven. Christ stands as King of Zion, presiding over and defending His church. The 144,000 are the same as in Revelation 7 — a remnant preserved from bowing to the beast. "His Father's name written on their foreheads" signifies adoption (the new name of a child of God), visible holiness, or open profession of faith — not baptism as some think. [biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/revelation/14.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/revelation/14.htm)

- **Ellicott:** It is "the Lamb" (with the article), the true Lamb of God against whom the wild beast wages war. Zion is the citadel of the heavenly city, introduced in contrast to Babylon (v. 8). The 144,000 is a symbolic number representing "the full growth of the choice ones of God, the true Israel of God." The name on their foreheads marks them as recognisable children of God. [biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/14.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/14.htm)

- **Guzik (Enduring Word):** These 144,000 are the same Jewish believers from Revelation 7 who minister during the Great Tribulation. Here they stand at the *end* of the Tribulation, triumphant. Mount Zion is the earthly Jerusalem where the Messiah will reign (citing Psalm 48, Isaiah 24:23, Joel 2:32, Obadiah 1:17, Micah 4:1-7). Some commentators view this as the heavenly Zion (Galatians 4:26), but Guzik rejects that — it would make God's seal on them pointless. The Father's name on their foreheads contrasts with the mark of the beast (Rev 13:16-17); the beast's mark is merely a counterfeit. [enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-14/](https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-14/)

- **Spurgeon (Baptist):** Zion was the dearest type of heaven to the Jewish mind. John's first and chief object of attention in heaven is "a Lamb!" — teaching that the central attraction of heaven is the person of Christ. The Lamb stands (posture of triumph), having conquered as a Lamb through sacrifice. [enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-14/](https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-14/) ; [studylight.org/commentaries/eng/spe/revelation-14.html](https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/spe/revelation-14.html)

**Precept Austin** (evangelical) provides an extensive discussion of whether this is earthly or heavenly Zion. Arguments for a heavenly scene: the 144,000 sing "before the throne, before the four living creatures and the elders" — always a heavenly location in Revelation. They are "redeemed from the earth," implying they are no longer on earth. Arguments for an earthly scene: God's seal protected them through the Tribulation; they enter the Millennial Kingdom as "firstfruits." A mediating view: John sees a preview of the earthly Millennial Zion while heavenly harpists sing. [preceptaustin.org/revelation-14-commentary](https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-14-commentary)

---

### v. 2: "And I heard a sound from heaven like the roar of many waters and the loud rumbling of thunder. And the sound I heard was like harpists strumming their harps."

- **Guzik:** "The voice of many waters and like loud thunder" is the voice of God (cf. Revelation 1:15, 4:5) — perhaps proclaiming approval of the 144,000. The harps may belong to the elders (Rev 5:8), accompanying the worship. [enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-14/](https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-14/)

- **Ellicott:** The voice from heaven blends majesty, terribleness, and sweetness — like sea and thunder blended with heavenly harps. He compares it to Psalm 29: the saints secure in Zion hear God's voice in thunder and sea all around them. [biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/14.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/14.htm)

- **Gill:** The voice like many waters is a great multitude (cf. Rev 17:15) praising God for antichrist's destruction. The thunder represents the Gospel's open, loud publication. The harps represent singing God's praises. He notes Brightman's historical interpretation: the church's voice was confused like waters in the wilderness period, then like thunder under the Waldenses and Wycliffe, then like harmonious harps at the Reformation. [biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/revelation/14.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/revelation/14.htm)

- **Precept Austin:** The MT/NU texts read "the voice which I heard was *like* harpists" — describing the quality of the sound, not necessarily literal harps. The singular "voice" could be God the Father's, since the Lamb is on Mount Zion. [preceptaustin.org/revelation-14-commentary](https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-14-commentary)

---

### v. 3: "And they sang a new song before the throne and before the four living creatures and the elders. And no one could learn the song except the 144,000 who had been redeemed from the earth."

- **Guzik:** Though their feet are on earthly Zion, their praise transports them before the throne of God. Only the 144,000 can learn this song because it comes from their unique experience of redemption through the Tribulation. Spurgeon is quoted: "Heaven is not the place to learn that song; it must be learned on the earth." [enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-14/](https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-14/)

- **Ellicott:** "They" (the singers) are the heavenly harpers, not the 144,000 themselves. It is a heavenly song, and "no spirit dulled by earthly desires can learn it." The redeemed — those "purchased from the earth" — can come with singing to Zion (cf. Isaiah 51:11). [biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/14.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/14.htm)

- **Gill:** The song is "the song of redeeming grace," the same as in Revelation 5:9. It is sung publicly in the church. Only the redeemed can sing it with experiential application — the natural man cannot learn it except in a merely notional way. [biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/revelation/14.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/revelation/14.htm)

- **Precept Austin:** There is debate about who sings. One view: the harpists in heaven sing *about* the 144,000, and the 144,000 on earth are the only ones who can *learn* it. The new song commemorates victory after conflict with dragon, beast, and false prophet — "never sung before, for such a conflict had never been fought before; therefore new." [preceptaustin.org/revelation-14-commentary](https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-14-commentary)

---

### v. 4: "These are the ones who have not been defiled with women, for they are virgins. They follow the Lamb wherever He goes. They have been redeemed from among men as firstfruits to God and to the Lamb."

**This verse is a significant point of interpretative divergence.**

- **Guzik (literal/celibacy view):** The 144,000 may be called to *literal* celibacy during the Great Tribulation. Paul recommended celibacy in distressing times (1 Corinthians 7:25-35), and Jesus spoke of woes on those with children in that day (Matthew 24:19-21). A.T. Robertson confirms that the Greek *parthenos* can apply to men as well as women. If "virgins" is figurative for spiritual purity, it still reinforces the connection with Israel — "the virgin daughter of Zion" is a frequent OT image (2 Kings 19:21, Isaiah 37:22, Lamentations 2:13, Jeremiah 18:13, Amos 5:2). The 144,000 are "firstfruits" — the godly nucleus of Israel, token of the nation's redemption, and possibly instrumental in bringing in the great ingathering of Revelation 7:9. [enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-14/](https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-14/)

- **Gill (spiritual purity view):** "Not defiled with women" means not defiled with the whore of Rome and her harlots — i.e., not involved in spiritual fornication (idolatry). "Virgins" refers to chastity, sincerity of love, uncorruptness in doctrine and worship, and uprightness of conversation (cf. Matthew 25:1). They "follow the Lamb wherever He goes" — as sheep follow the shepherd (John 10:4), in graces, duties, sufferings, and into heaven. "Firstfruits" alludes to the OT law: the firstfruits sanctified the lump and foreshadowed the coming harvest. These are the first converts in the period preceding Christ's spiritual reign. [biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/revelation/14.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/revelation/14.htm)

- **Ellicott (purity of heart view):** "The expression can hardly be limited to the unmarried, as the 144,000 represent the wide society of the choice ones of God." They are those with the purity of heart Christ blessed (Matthew 5:8) — the first mark of heavenly wisdom (James 3:17). "They follow the Lamb wherever He goes" describes complete consecration, not merely a heavenly reward. It echoes Christ's words: "Whosoever forsaketh not all he hath cannot be My disciple." [biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/14.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/14.htm)

---

### v. 5: "And no lie was found in their mouths; they are blameless."

- **Gill:** "No guile" (most manuscripts) means no idolatry (idols are often called "lies" in the OT, e.g., Jeremiah 16:19), no false doctrine, no hypocrisy. "Without fault" — not sinless in themselves, but washed in Christ's blood, justified by His righteousness, and thus unblamable before God (cf. Colossians 1:22). [biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/revelation/14.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/revelation/14.htm)

- **Ellicott:** Utter truthfulness is their fourth distinguishing feature. The words "before the throne of God" must be omitted (a textual variant — they are absent from key manuscripts). They are "blameless" (cf. Revelation 7:14-15; Ephesians 5:27; Colossians 1:22). [biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/14.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/14.htm)

- **Precept Austin:** "Without fault" (Greek *amōmoi*) — the same word used of Christ as the spotless Lamb (1 Peter 1:19). It describes their position in Christ rather than inherent sinlessness. [preceptaustin.org/revelation-14-commentary](https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-14-commentary)

---

### vv. 6–7: The First Angel — The Eternal Gospel

**v. 6:** "Then I saw another angel flying overhead, with the eternal gospel to proclaim to those who dwell on the earth—to every nation and tribe and tongue and people."

- **Guzik:** This angel preaches the gospel *and* announces judgment. Some have tried to identify this angel with modern technology or ministries — Adam Clarke (18th century) thought it was the British and Foreign Bible Society; John Trapp (17th century) thought it was John Wycliffe. These identifications miss the point. This is the only place in the NT where angels preach the gospel; normally God gives that responsibility to His people. [enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-14/](https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-14/)

- **Gill:** "Another angel" means a minister of the Gospel, not a literal angel — in Revelation, pastors are called "angels" (Rev 1:20). It is a *set* of Gospel ministers appearing at the beginning of Christ's spiritual reign. The Gospel is "everlasting" because its substance was settled from eternity, its matter is eternal (election, covenant, righteousness, life), and it will abide forever. [biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/revelation/14.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/revelation/14.htm)

- **Ellicott:** The angel flies "in mid-heaven" — the gospel is proclaimed in view of all nations. The term "everlasting gospel" (or "an eternal gospel") means the good news that God loves the world, has redeemed mankind. This word is the sword of the Spirit, the Church's weapon against her foes. [biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/14.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/14.htm)

**v. 7:** "And he said in a loud voice, 'Fear God and give Him glory, because the hour of His judgment has come. Worship the One who made the heavens and the earth and the sea and the springs of waters.'"

- **Guzik:** The call to "fear God and give Him glory" is an appeal to do willingly now what all will be compelled to do later (Philippians 2:9-11). "Here is the bitter irony of their lot: though they damn themselves eternally by their refusal to face the truth, one day they will be forced to face it" (Kiddle). The wording sounds different from our gospel today, but it is "the Gospel in the form it takes when the hour of judgment has set in" (Seiss). [enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-14/](https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-14/)

- **Gill:** "Fear God" means not the beast, nor with servile or hypocritical fear, but with godly, reverential fear springing from a sense of God's love. The "hour of His judgment" is not the last judgment but the commencement of Christ's spiritual reign — His time to judge antichrist and avenge His people (cf. Revelation 11:15). [biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/revelation/14.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/revelation/14.htm)

- **Precept Austin:** The angel's words are a *summary* of the required response to the gospel, not the full gospel message itself. Those who respond in faith are found in Revelation 15:3-4 doing precisely this: fearing God, glorifying Him, and declaring His works. [preceptaustin.org/revelation-14-commentary](https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-14-commentary)

---

### v. 8: The Second Angel — Fall of Babylon

"And a second angel followed, saying, 'Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great, who has made all the nations drink the wine of the passion of her immorality.'"

- **Guzik:** More on Babylon comes in Revelation 17. For now, it represents "mankind in organized rebellion against God." Walvoord notes that "Babylon" can refer to a literal city, a religious system, or a political system — all deriving from historic Babylon's evil character. The "fornication" is primarily spiritual (worship of other gods), though often accompanied by literal immorality. [enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-14/](https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-14/)

- **Ellicott:** The second angel follows the first: the doom of the world-city follows the proclamation of the gospel. "Babylon belongs not to one age." Pagan Rome was Babylon to John; papal Rome was Babylon to a later age (Dante, Savonarola, Luther). Babylon has reared palaces on the Seine, Thames, Tiber, and Bosphorus. The gospel will cast down everything that exalts itself against the knowledge of God. [biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/14.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/14.htm)

- **Gill:** This announces the fall of Rome — both pagan and papal. The "wine of the wrath of her fornication" means her idolatrous practices that intoxicate and madden the nations, drawing them into both sin and its consequent judgment. [biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/revelation/14.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/revelation/14.htm)

---

### vv. 9–11: The Third Angel — Warning Against the Beast

**v. 9:** "And a third angel followed them, calling out in a loud voice, 'If anyone worships the beast and its image, and receives its mark on his forehead or on his hand...'"

- **Guzik:** There is a deliberate connection between worshipping the beast and receiving his mark — no one will casually or accidentally take it. To those on earth, it may seem like a mere pledge of allegiance (like burning incense to Caesar in the early centuries), but the spiritual reality is deadly serious. [enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-14/](https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-14/)

- **Ellicott:** The warning declares individual human responsibility — "there is no necessity for his receiving the mark, the hall-mark of a cowardly connivance at wrong-doing, or for setting his judgments by the fashions of the world." [biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/14.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/14.htm)

**v. 10:** "he too will drink the wine of God's anger, poured undiluted into the cup of His wrath. And he will be tormented in fire and sulfur in the presence of the holy angels and of the Lamb."

- **Guzik:** Two Greek words for anger appear: *thymos* (passionate anger — the "wine") and *orge* (settled disposition — the "cup"). Normally God's anger is described as *orge*; but in Revelation, which depicts ultimate judgment, *thymos* is used much more frequently (10 of its 11 NT occurrences). The cup is "poured undiluted" — mixed with spices to make it stronger. Jesus voluntarily took this cup for us (Matthew 26:39); His enemies have it forced on them. [enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-14/](https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-14/)

- **Ellicott:** "He shall have judgment without mercy that hath showed no mercy" (James 2:13). The wine is "mingled pure" — in full strength, undiluted. [biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/14.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/14.htm)

- **Guzik on torment "in the presence of the Lamb":** God is *not* absent from hell. He is present in all His holiness and righteous judgment. Hell will not be devoid of God's presence, but it will be without any sense of His love. The presence of Jesus there is the presence of His holy justice and wrath. [enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-14/](https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-14/)

**v. 11:** "And the smoke of their torment rises forever and ever. Day and night there is no rest for those who worship the beast and its image, or for anyone who receives the mark of its name."

- **Guzik:** "Forever and ever" is literally "into the ages of ages" — the strongest expression of eternity Greek can produce (Walvoord). The present tense in "worship" and "receive" indicates continued, unrepentant worship; likewise the present tense of the torment indicates it is uninterrupted. "The modern vogue for dispensing with hell has no counterpart in Revelation" (L. Morris). [enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-14/](https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-14/)

- **Ellicott:** The imagery of smoke recalls the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah (Genesis 19:28; Isaiah 34:10). "Sin, which is first embraced as a delight, becomes soon an inexorable tyrant... There is a destiny of unrest in all sin. 'The wicked are like the troubled sea, which cannot rest.'" [biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/14.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/14.htm)

---

### v. 12: "Here is a call for the perseverance of the saints who keep the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus."

- **Guzik:** This verse contrasts the rest of the saints with the ceaseless torment of the wicked (v. 11). The rest comes through patient endurance and faithfulness. [enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-14/](https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-14/)

- **Ellicott:** "Here is the patience of the saints who keep..." — not "here are they." The patience (endurance) of the saints is seen precisely in this readiness to wait, to endure tribulation, to keep God's commandments, and to refuse homage to the god of this world because of faith that Jesus is King. [biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/14.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/14.htm)

---

### v. 13: "And I heard a voice from heaven telling me to write, 'Blessed are the dead—those who die in the Lord from this moment on.' 'Yes,' says the Spirit, 'they will rest from their labors, for their deeds will follow them.'"

- **Guzik:** This is the second of seven beatitudes in Revelation. It gives courage to tribulation saints facing martyrdom. "Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord" — Clarke calls them "the only glorious dead... they die in the cause of God, they die under the smile and approbation of God, and they die to live and reign with God forever." Their works follow them — giving eternal dignity to faithful labour here below. [enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-14/](https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-14/)

- **Ellicott:** The blessing is not only for martyrs but for *all* who die "in the Lord" — in happy union and fellowship with Him (John 15:2-5; 1 John 1:3). "From henceforth" reflects the state of trouble just described: the righteous are happy to be taken away from the evil to come. Or it may console mourners in an age when "dark unbelief robs away the sweet resurrection trust, and writes over its graves, 'Farewell for ever.'" Their works "follow with them" into the presence of their Lord. [biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/14.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/14.htm)

- **Spurgeon** (cited in Enduring Word): "To be rapt in praise to God is the highest state of the soul... praise is heaven, and heaven is praise! To pray is heaven below, but praise is the essence of heaven above." [enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-14/](https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-14/)

---

### vv. 14–16: The Harvest of the Earth (Righteous)

**v. 14:** "And I looked and saw a white cloud, and seated on the cloud was One like the Son of Man, with a golden crown on His head and a sharp sickle in His hand."

- **Guzik:** The "One like the Son of Man" is undeniably Jesus (cf. Daniel 7:13; Matthew 26:64). Some struggle with Jesus responding to an angel's command, but no one else is called "Son of Man" and wears a golden crown. The crown (*stephanos*) is the victor's crown, not the royal diadem — Christ comes to judge wearing the garland He won in conflict. [enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-14/](https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-14/)

- **Ellicott:** The cloud (Matthew 24:30; Acts 1:9), "Son of Man" (John 5:27; Daniel 7:13), the crown, and resemblance to Revelation 1 confirm Christ is intended. The crown is the crown of victory; the sickle signals that harvest has come (cf. Joel 3:12-14; Mark 4:26-29). [biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/14.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/14.htm)

**v. 15:** "Then another angel came out of the temple, crying out in a loud voice to the One seated on the cloud, 'Swing Your sickle and reap, because the time has come to harvest; for the crop of the earth is ripe.'"

- **Ellicott:** This is the harvest of the *good seed* — the full corn in the ear gathered into the celestial garner (Mark 4:26-29). Significantly, the angel who announces the harvest comes from the *temple* (the inner shrine measured off in Revelation 11:1), while the angel who calls for the vintage comes from the *altar* (pointing to judgment). The wheat stalks are "dry" — the fields white for harvest (John 4:35). [biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/14.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/14.htm)

- **Precept Austin:** The Son of Man is the one who reaps the harvest of the saved — He sowed the good seed (Matthew 13:37) and now He reaps. Angels carry out the details, but Christ is intimately involved in this harvest. One view connects this with the resurrection of tribulation saints prior to the Millennial Kingdom (cf. Revelation 20:4). [preceptaustin.org/revelation-14-commentary](https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-14-commentary)

**v. 16:** "So the One seated on the cloud swung His sickle over the earth, and the earth was harvested."

- **Guzik:** The ancient Greek word for "ripe" implies the harvest is over-ripe — it *must* happen now. Jesus reaps the righteous; an angel reaps the wicked (vv. 17-20). [enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-14/](https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-14/)

---

### vv. 17–20: The Vintage of Wrath (Wicked)

**v. 17:** "Then another angel came out of the temple in heaven, and he too had a sharp sickle."

- **Ellicott:** This angel also has a sharp sickle (like the Son of Man), but he comes for a different harvest — the vintage of judgment. [biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/14.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/14.htm)

**v. 18:** "Still another angel, with authority over the fire, came from the altar and called out in a loud voice to the angel with the sharp sickle, 'Swing your sharp sickle and gather the clusters of grapes from the vine of the earth, because its grapes are ripe.'"

- **Ellicott:** This angel comes from the *altar* — beneath which the martyred saints had cried "How long?" (Revelation 6:9-10). He has authority over the fire (cf. Revelation 8:5, where the angel mingled incense with the prayers of the saints and flung fire toward the earth). Now he proclaims: the hour of vengeance has come! The angel who receives the call comes from the temple — "as one who has witnessed their secret sorrows and their sufferings, and is fitted to recompense tribulation to the troublers of Israel" (2 Thessalonians 1:6). [biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/14.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/14.htm)

- **Precept Austin:** This is the answer to the martyrs' cry of "How long?" from Revelation 6:10. The angel with authority over fire comes from the very altar associated with those prayers. [preceptaustin.org/revelation-14-commentary](https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-14-commentary)

**v. 19:** "So the angel swung his sickle over the earth and gathered the grapes of the earth, and he threw them into the great winepress of God's wrath."

- **Ellicott:** The treading of the winepress is a figure of vengeance; the red juice of the grape strongly suggests the shedding of blood (cf. Isaiah 63:2-4). [biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/14.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/14.htm)

**v. 20:** "And the winepress was trodden outside the city, and the blood that flowed from it rose as high as the bridles of the horses for a distance of 1,600 stadia."

- **Ellicott:** Winepresses stood outside the city — here it signifies that those under judgment refused the defence of the true city and sanctuary (cf. v. 1 and Psalm 132:17-18). The 1,600 stadia (about 180 miles / 300 km) is symbolic: 4 × 4 × 100, representing judgment complete and full, reaching to all corners of the earth. "The whole world, of which Satan is called the prince, is judged, and condemned, and punished" (Dr. Currey). [biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/14.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/14.htm)

- **Guzik:** The vivid description of blood up to horses' bridles shows how complete God's judgment is. Revelation 14 is the answer to Revelation 13: at the end of chapter 13 it almost seemed Satan and the Antichrist might win, but chapter 14 shows who is really triumphant. [enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-14/](https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-14/)

- **Precept Austin:** 1,600 stadia is approximately the length of the land of Israel from north to south — suggesting judgment focused on the land, or symbolically worldwide. [preceptaustin.org/revelation-14-commentary](https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-14-commentary)

## Traditions Compared

### Where Protestant Traditions Differ on Key Verses

**The 144,000 (vv. 1–5):**

- **Dispensational premillennial (Guzik, Precept Austin's main line):** The 144,000 are literal Jewish believers, 12,000 from each tribe, who evangelise during the Tribulation and survive to enter the Millennial Kingdom. They are on *earthly* Mount Zion. [enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-14/](https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-14/)

- **Historicist/Amillennial (Gill, Ellicott in part):** The 144,000 are symbolic of the whole body of the redeemed — "the true Israel of God." Mount Zion is the church. Gill explicitly says Mount Zion means "not heaven, but the church on earth." [biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/revelation/14.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/revelation/14.htm) ; [biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/14.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/14.htm)

- **Reformed/Amillennial** (Spurgeon): The 144,000 represent "all the chosen race" — the number is symbolic. He explicitly says "the number typified by that number." Denominational labels vanish; only the Father's name matters. [studylight.org/commentaries/eng/spe/revelation-14.html](https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/spe/revelation-14.html)

**"Not defiled with women... for they are virgins" (v. 4):**

- **Literal celibacy view (Guzik/Pentecostal-charismatic):** The 144,000 are called to literal sexual abstinence during the Tribulation. [enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-14/](https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-14/)

- **Spiritual purity view (Gill/Baptist, Ellicott/Anglican):** "Virgins" means purity from spiritual fornication (idolatry, false worship). Gill applies it to freedom from Rome's corruption. Ellicott says it means purity of heart and "can hardly be limited to the unmarried." [biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/revelation/14.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/revelation/14.htm) ; [biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/14.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/14.htm)

**The angel preaching the "everlasting gospel" (vv. 6–7):**

- **Gill (Baptist/Historicist):** The "angel" is not a literal angel but Gospel ministers — pastors are called "angels" in Revelation 1:20. This refers to a future set of preachers ushering in Christ's spiritual reign. [biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/revelation/14.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/revelation/14.htm)

- **Guzik (Dispensational):** A literal angel preaches — the only instance of angelic evangelism in the NT, fulfilling Matthew 24:14 during the Tribulation. This does *not* excuse the Church from missions. [enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-14/](https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-14/)

**The harvests (vv. 14–20):** All traditional commentators agree there are two distinct harvests: the grain harvest (righteous, reaped by Christ) and the grape harvest (wicked, reaped by an angel into the winepress of wrath). Ellicott contrasts them as the "autumn gladness" of harvest versus the "tokens of judgment" in the vintage. [biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/14.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/14.htm)
